headline: This law directs NOAA to create an advisory committee that helps guide a federal grant program for fisheries research and development.
what_it_does: The law requires the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) to set up the American Fisheries Advisory Committee. The committee advises NOAA on an existing grant program that funds fisheries research and development projects, such as fisheries science and recreational fishing. Its duties include identifying the needs of the fishing community, helping write the grant request for proposals, reviewing grant applications, and giving NOAA applications for approval. NOAA must divide the committee into six regions and choose members from those regions, plus at-large members who represent certain parts of the fishing industry.

who_it_affects.how: They gain a formal committee that represents their needs when federal fisheries research grants are designed and reviewed.
People chosen from each of the six regions and from certain fishing-industry sectors take on advisory roles on the committee.

who_it_affects.group: Organizations applying for NOAA fisheries research grants
who_it_affects.how: Their grant applications will be reviewed first by the committee before NOAA makes a final decision.

when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on May 12, 2022; the summary does not state a specific effective date or deadline for forming the committee.
